raw.transcript: First, restart your router and modem by unplugging them for about 10 seconds, then plug them back in and wait for the lights to stabilize. Next, move closer to the router and test if the drops still happen, since distance and walls can weaken the signal. Then on your device, turn Wi-Fi off and back on, and remove any old duplicate networks so it reconnects cleanly. After that, check for router firmware updates in the router’s admin page and install any available updates. Then change the Wi-Fi channel or switch from a crowded 2.4 gigahertz band to 5 gigahertz if your devices support it. Finally, temporarily disable any VPN or security app that might interfere, and if drops continue across multiple devices, contact your internet provider to check for line issues.
